Medford at a glance

Selling in Medford?

Get My Cash Offer →

Where is Medford, Oregon, and what is the land like?

Medford is the county seat of Jackson County, in the Rogue Valley about 27 miles north of the California border. It sits at 1,434 feet in a rain shadow between the Cascade Range and the Siskiyou Mountains, which explains the dry summers.

Roxy Ann Peak rises to 3,576 feet at the edge of town, and Prescott Park around it covers 1,740 acres. Bear Creek Park runs nearly 100 acres, and Alba Park, deeded to the city in 1888, is the oldest. Houses on the foothills and houses on the valley floor face different slopes, drainage and fire exposure, so describe the lot as well as the building.

How did Medford get its start?

Medford began as a railroad survey stop. Surveyors working on the Oregon and California Railroad route in 1883 included David Loring, who named the town for Medford, Massachusetts.

  • The town was platted in early December 1883 with 82 blocks.
  • The first post office opened February 6, 1884.
  • Medford incorporated as a town on February 24, 1885, and as a city in 1905.
  • It took the county seat from Jacksonville in 1927.
  • Interstate 5 was completed through town in 1967.

That timeline matters for sellers because it explains the mix of old railroad-era streets near downtown and newer subdivisions farther out.

What does Medford's population look like?

Medford is the eighth-largest city in Oregon and the largest in Jackson County. The 2020 census counted 85,824 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 86,494 as of July 1, 2025.

Which employers drive the Medford economy?

Health care is the largest driver. Asante Rogue Regional Medical Center and Providence Medford Medical Center together employ more than 2,000 people.

  • Harry and David is described as the largest employer in Southern Oregon, with about 1,700 year-round and 6,700 seasonal workers.
  • Lithia Motors, a Fortune 500 company, has been headquartered in Medford since 1970.
  • Jackson County has more than 10,000 acres of orchards and shares the Rogue Valley and Applegate wine appellations with Josephine County.

With seasonal work at Harry and David and shift work in health care, a rental's tenant mix can turn over on a different calendar than a typical house, so check lease end dates before you set a closing date.

How hot and dry does Medford get, and what does that do to a house?

Medford has a Mediterranean climate with hot summers and dry air. Summers average 61 afternoons above 90 degrees and 11 above 100, and the record high is 115 degrees, reached July 20, 1946 and again June 28, 2021.

Annual precipitation averages 18.43 inches and snowfall 3.4 inches. Winter temperature inversions can hold fog in the valley for weeks. Long hot spells age roofing, exterior paint and air conditioning equipment, and a buyer's inspector will look at all three.

How did the Almeda fire affect Medford housing?

The Almeda fire started the morning of September 8, 2020, and swept through the Rogue Valley within hours. Jefferson Public Radio reported more than 2,600 homes destroyed between Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, calling it the most destructive wildfire in Oregon's recorded history.

Medford lost homes too, including a mobile home park in the city. A year later, thousands of displaced residents had not received the federal help they needed to rebuild. For a seller, the effects show up in two ways:

  • Fire-damaged or rebuilt properties may carry insurance, permit or valuation questions that a buyer will ask about.
  • Under ORS 308.146, a fire or other act of God that cuts a property's real market value also reduces its maximum assessed value for that year.

Oregon lawmakers passed a bill in 2025 to repeal the state's contested wildfire hazard map, which the statewide defensible space and building code requirements relied on. A 2023 state law still bars insurers from using a state agency's wildfire hazard map to cancel, decline to renew or raise premiums on a homeowner policy.

How do Medford's highways, buses and airport work?

Interstate 5 runs through the center of Medford, including a 3,229-foot viaduct, and Highways 99, 62 and 238 also serve the city. Rogue Valley International-Medford Airport is Oregon's third-busiest and handles over a million passengers a year on about 60 daily flights.

The Rogue Valley Transportation District has run buses since 1975 and operates eight routes. There is no passenger train service, and the last direct rail service to Portland ended in 1956. Buyers who rely on the bus or the airport may care how close a house is to those lines.

How does Medford fit into the wider Rogue Valley?

Medford is the largest of Jackson County's 11 incorporated cities. The county covers 2,802 square miles, and nearby towns include Ashland, Phoenix, Talent, Central Point and Jacksonville.

Jacksonville was the first county seat, from 1853, and lost ground after the railroad bypassed it. Bear Creek and its watershed lie wholly inside the county and drain to the Rogue River. Buyers often compare Medford with those neighbors, so know what sets your street apart.

What schools serve Medford?

Medford School District 549C serves the city, with more than 13,000 students as of 2012. It runs North Medford, South Medford and Central Medford high schools plus Medford Innovation Academy, three middle schools (Hedrick, Oakdale and McLoughlin) and 14 elementary schools.

Private schools include St. Mary's, Cascade Christian, Crossroads and Rogue Valley Adventist. Rogue Community College opened a downtown campus in 1997. Confirm current boundaries with the district before you cite a school in a listing.

What do Census figures say about Medford housing?

Medford has a lower owner-occupancy rate than nearby McMinnville or Oregon City, at 56.3%. That leaves a large renter base and many landlord-owned houses.

Who handles property tax in Medford?

Jackson County bills Medford property tax, and the Assessor's Office can be reached at 541-774-6059. The county's address is 10 S Oakdale Ave in Medford.

State law sets the schedule: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Pay by November 15 and you get 3% off the full bill or 2% off if you pay two-thirds. Unpaid balances accrue interest at 1 1/3% per month. ORS 306.815 generally bars cities and counties from taxing transfers of real property, with narrow exceptions, so ask your title company to confirm there is no local transfer charge on your sale.

What do Medford sellers need to plan for?

  • A signed disclosure statement for each buyer who makes a written offer, unless the sale is excluded, for example a court-appointed personal representative selling an estate.
  • Smoke, heat or fire history that insurers or buyers may ask about.
  • Tenant notice and move-out timing if the house is a rental.
  • Proration of the current tax year at closing.

A cash buyer can often work around a house's condition, but each buyer sets its own terms, so compare them in writing.

More questions about Medford, OR

What county is Medford, Oregon in?

Medford is in Jackson County and has been the county seat since 1927. Property tax questions go to the Jackson County Assessor's Office.

How many people live in Medford?

The Census Bureau estimates 86,494 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 85,824.

Was Medford affected by the Almeda fire?

Yes. The fire began September 8, 2020, and destroyed more than 2,600 homes across Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, including a mobile home park in Medford.

When are property taxes due in Jackson County?

The three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. Paying in full by November 15 earns a 3% discount.

Does Medford charge a real estate transfer tax?

Generally no. ORS 306.815 bars cities and counties from imposing a transfer tax, with narrow exceptions tied to rules in place on March 31, 1997 or to low recording fees. Your title company can confirm for your sale.

Can I sell a Medford rental with tenants in it?

Yes. Many buyers accept occupied houses, but notice rules and lease terms still apply, so confirm them before you set a closing date.

Oregon City at a glance

Selling in Oregon City?

Where is Oregon City, and why does its terrain matter?

Oregon City is the county seat of Clackamas County, on the Willamette River near the southern edge of the Portland metro area. The city sits at 466 feet and is built in two tiers: a lower area on a bench beside the river and an upper area on a basalt bluff.

The Willamette forms the boundary with West Linn, and the Clackamas River forms the boundary with Gladstone. A water-powered elevator linked the two tiers in 1915, was converted to electricity in the 1920s and replaced by a new electric elevator in 1952. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. If your house is on the bluff, say so, since buyers care about slope, views and walking access.

Which Oregon City neighborhoods come up most?

The city lists 12 official neighborhood associations. Three areas stand out in descriptions of the city.

  • McLoughlin sits on the bluff above downtown and has many older homes, the McLoughlin House, the public library, a pool and a hospital.
  • Canemah is a narrow strip between the Willamette and a bluff along OR 99E. It was founded in 1845 as an independent city, served as the portage site around the falls, and was later annexed.
  • Two Rivers is the lowest part of the city and mostly commercial, including downtown and Clackamette Park.

What is Oregon City's history?

Oregon City was the end of the Oregon Trail and the first U.S. city west of the Rocky Mountains to incorporate. Dr. John McLoughlin of the Hudson's Bay Company founded the settlement in 1829 to use Willamette Falls to power a lumber mill, and the city incorporated in 1844.

  • It was the capital of Oregon Territory from 1848 to 1851.
  • The Oregon Spectator, published in 1846, was the first American newspaper west of the Rockies.
  • In 1889 the city began the first long-distance electrical service in the country, sending power 14 miles to Portland.
  • The Willamette Falls Locks, in West Linn, were the first multi-lift navigational locks in the U.S.

How big is Oregon City, and who lives there?

The Census Bureau estimates 38,175 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 37,572 in the 2020 census. In 2020 there were 13,966 households and the median age was 38.2.

Oregon City's 65.3% ownership rate and $555,800 median home value are higher than the McMinnville, Medford and Newberg figures, and only 14.7% of its residents are 65 or older.

What does the Oregon City economy rely on?

Forestry dominated the city's history until the Pacific Northwest lumber industry declined starting in the 1980s, and today Oregon City is largely a Portland suburb. The last paper mill in the immediate area closed in 2017 and reopened in 2019 under new ownership.

Tourism built on history is growing, centered on the Willamette Falls Legacy Project, a planned public-access, mixed-use redevelopment of the falls area. Clackamas Community College is in the city. The End of the Oregon Trail Interpretive Center closed in September 2009 over funding and reopened in summer 2013. Other sites include the Museum of the Oregon Territory, the 1908 Stevens-Crawford Heritage House Museum, the Ermatinger House, the oldest in Clackamas County, and the 1922 Oregon City Bridge.

What does the weather mean for an Oregon City house?

Oregon City has hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters, with most of its 44.81 inches of annual rain falling from November to March. The annual average temperature is 55.4 degrees, and December averages 41.8.

The record high is 114 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and the record low is minus 2, on January 31, 1950. A wet half of the year is hard on roofs, decks and retaining walls, and bluff lots add drainage to the list of things a buyer will check.

How do roads, trains and buses serve Oregon City?

Interstate 205 crosses the northern edge of the city and is the only freeway serving it. Oregon Routes 43, 99E and 213 pass through or end in town.

  • Amtrak Cascades trains stop twice daily in each direction between Portland and Eugene, while the Coast Starlight passes without stopping.
  • TriMet buses converge at the Oregon City Transit Center, with added service from South Clackamas Transportation District and Canby Area Transit.
  • There is no public airport in the city. Portland International is about 15 miles north.

Which schools serve Oregon City?

The Oregon City School District has seven elementary schools, two middle schools, Oregon City High School and an alternative secondary school. Several schools offer bilingual English and Spanish programs. Oregon City High School is described as the third most populated high school in Oregon.

What do Oregon City historic districts mean for a seller?

If your house is in a designated historic area, exterior changes need city review before work starts. Oregon City's list includes the Canemah National Register District and the McLoughlin Conservation District, which spans streets from 1st through 12th.

  • Windows, doors, siding changes and additions to designated structures need special review.
  • Type I review is a staff decision for limited alterations that meet clear policies.
  • Type III review goes to the Historic Review Board for discretionary decisions, additions under 30% of the original structure, and new construction or larger additions.

Planning staff can say whether a property is designated at ocplanning@orcity.org or 503-722-3789. A buyer who plans changes will ask, so find out before you list.

How are Clackamas County property taxes billed for an Oregon City house?

Clackamas County's Department of Assessment and Taxation bills Oregon City property from its office at 150 Beavercreek Road, Suite 135, phone 503-655-8671. For 2025 it issued 170,621 statements totaling $1,235,352,377, up 5.02% from the prior year.

State law sets installments for November 15, February 15 and May 15. In 2025 the county listed the first deadline as November 17, with a 3% discount for payment in full and 2% for two-thirds, and the later installments February 17, 2026 and May 15, 2026. Value appeals went to the Property Value Appeals Board by December 31, 2025. Ask the title company to settle the current installment at closing.

What disclosure and sale rules should an Oregon City seller know?

Sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must give a signed disclosure statement to each buyer who makes a written offer, and a buyer has five business days after delivery to revoke unless they waived that right. Court-appointed sellers, such as personal representatives and trustees, and foreclosing financial institutions are excluded under ORS 105.470.

Oregon City sellers weigh a listing, a sale on their own and an as-is cash sale. A cash buyer sets its own terms, so compare timelines, repair responsibility and closing costs in writing.

More questions about Oregon City, OR

What county is Oregon City in?

Clackamas County. Oregon City is the county seat, and the county's assessment and taxation office is in the city.

How many people live in Oregon City?

The Census Bureau estimates 38,175 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 37,572.

Why is Oregon City important in Oregon history?

It was the end of the Oregon Trail, the first U.S. city west of the Rockies to incorporate in 1844, and capital of Oregon Territory from 1848 to 1851.

Do Oregon City historic district rules affect selling?

They can. Exterior changes to designated structures need staff or Historic Review Board review, so a buyer who wants to alter a Canemah or McLoughlin house will ask about it.

When are property taxes due in Clackamas County?

State law sets November 15, February 15 and May 15. In 2025 the county listed November 17 for the first deadline, with a 3% discount for payment in full.

What is the median home value in Oregon City?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied units is $555,800. It is a city-wide median, not a value for one house.

Where is McMinnville and how is the city laid out?

McMinnville is the county seat and largest city of Yamhill County, in the Willamette Valley at the foot of the Oregon Coast Range. It sits where the North and South forks of the Yamhill River meet, about 37 miles southwest of Portland and 26 miles northwest of Salem, at 161 feet above sea level.

The city covers 10.58 square miles, all of it land. Downtown runs along East Third Street, the older residential streets spread west along West Second Street, and collector roads such as Baker Creek Road and Cypress Street tie the outer residential and industrial areas together. A house on the west side and one near the highway corridor can sell to very different buyers, so the street matters as much as the city name.

How did McMinnville grow into a city of about 34,000?

McMinnville began with a land claim. William T. Newby claimed the site in 1844, built a grist mill in 1853, and platted the town on May 5, 1856, naming it for his hometown of McMinnville, Tennessee. The plat was not recorded until July 1865.

The town incorporated in 1876 and became a city in 1882. Voters moved the county seat here from Lafayette in 1886, which is why county offices and courts are in town today.

MeasureMcMinnville figure
Population, 2000 census26,499

What jobs and industries support McMinnville homeowners?

Health care, higher education and manufacturing anchor the local job base. The 2020 list of top employers named Willamette Valley Medical Center, Linfield University and Cascade Steel Rolling Mills.

  • Linfield University opened in 1858 as the Baptist College of McMinnville, took its current name in 2020, and enrolls about 2,000 students on nearly 200 acres.
  • Cascade Steel makes finished steel from recycled scrap and is a subsidiary of Radius Recycling.
  • Oregon Mutual Insurance dates to 1894, and First Federal Savings and Loan was founded here in 1922.
  • Organic Valley bought the Farmers Cooperative Creamery in 2016. A 2021 fire destroyed the plant, and it was rebuilt and reopened.

Wine adds another layer. The McMinnville AVA was established in January 2005 and covers 14 wineries and 523 acres within the Willamette Valley AVA. Yamhill County has the largest vineyard area of any Oregon county. A seller whose house sits near vineyard land or the downtown tasting rooms is selling into that setting.

What does McMinnville's climate mean for an older house?

McMinnville has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate, so the main wear on a house comes from a long wet season. Monthly mean temperatures run from 40.5 degrees in December to 67.5 degrees in August, and rain averages 37.64 inches a year with November the wettest month.

The extremes are real but rare. The record high is 114 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and the record low is minus 7 degrees on January 31, 1950. Marine fog from the coast is common. Roofs, gutters, siding and crawl spaces take the brunt of months of damp, so those are worth a look before a buyer does.

How do roads, rail and the airport shape McMinnville real estate?

Oregon Route 99W runs through the city, Oregon Route 18 bypasses it to the south and leads to the coast, and Route 47 begins just northeast of the city limits. Newberg and Portland are reachable along 99W, which matters for sellers whose buyers commute.

  • McMinnville Municipal Airport is city-owned, and the Oregon International Air Show has been held there each September since 2019.
  • The Portland & Western Railroad has served the city since 1993 on a line leased from Union Pacific.
  • Yamhill County Transit Area runs public transit.
  • The Evergreen Aviation & Space Museum, home of the Spruce Goose, is reached from the same Route 18 corridor as the airport.

Who provides power, water and sewer in McMinnville?

McMinnville Water and Light, a city-owned utility, handles electric and water service. Its main office is at 340 NE Kirby Street, and the phone number is (503) 472-6158.

The utility reports an electric territory of 75 square miles and 162 miles of water main. Residential sewer charges are based on water use from November through March. A seller moving out should call the office to set a final meter reading and a date to transfer service, since the utility's site does not spell out the steps for a sale.

What are McMinnville's schools and colleges?

The McMinnville School District serves about 7,000 students in kindergarten through grade 12. It runs five elementary schools, two middle schools and McMinnville High School, which has more than 2,000 students. Private options include McMinnville Montessori School, McMinnville Christian Academy and St. James Catholic Elementary School.

Chemeketa Community College has had a Yamhill Valley campus here with accreditation since 2011. Check attendance boundaries with the district before you describe a house as being in a particular school area.

What do Census numbers say about McMinnville housing?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates show a city where most households own, with a median home value of $432,800. The figures below are survey estimates for the whole city, not a price for any one house.

About one resident in five is 65 or older, so downsizing and inherited houses are part of the local picture.

When are property taxes due on a McMinnville house?

Oregon bills property tax in three installments, due November 15, February 15 and May 15. Yamhill County, where McMinnville sits, collects the bill.

  • Paying everything by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and paying two-thirds by then earns 2%.
  • Late amounts accrue interest of 1 1/3% per month, starting after December 15 for the first installment.
  • Under ORS 308.146, taxable value generally grows no faster than 3% a year unless the property changes, so a buyer's bill can differ from the seller's.

Ask the title company to prorate the current year's tax at closing.

What must a McMinnville seller disclose?

Most Oregon sellers of one-to-four-unit homes must give each buyer who makes a written offer a signed seller's property disclosure statement. A buyer who receives it can revoke the offer within five business days unless a written waiver was already delivered.

Some sales are excluded under ORS 105.470, including sales by court-appointed personal representatives and trustees and sales by a financial institution that took the property through foreclosure. If you are selling an inherited house, ask the estate's attorney whether the exclusion applies.

What sellers in McMinnville usually weigh

Sellers here usually compare three routes: listing with an agent, selling without one, or accepting an as-is offer from a cash buyer. A cash buyer sets its own terms and timeline, so compare more than the headline number.

  • Condition: wet-season roof, gutter and crawl-space wear is common in older houses.
  • Timing: tax installments, utility transfer and any move-out date.
  • Paperwork: the disclosure statement, or the estate exclusion if it applies.
  • Costs: who pays for repairs, title and closing.

More questions about McMinnville, OR

How many people live in McMinnville?

The Census Bureau estimates 34,647 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 34,319.

Which county is McMinnville in?

Yamhill County. McMinnville is its county seat and its largest city, so the assessor and tax office serving your house are the county's.

When are Oregon property taxes due?

The three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. A 3% discount applies if you pay in full by November 15.

Do I have to give a disclosure statement when I sell in McMinnville?

Usually yes for a one-to-four-unit home, with exclusions such as court-appointed sellers and foreclosing financial institutions. A buyer who gets the statement has five business days to revoke the offer unless they waived that right.

Who do I call to stop utilities when I sell?

Call McMinnville Water and Light at (503) 472-6158 to schedule a final reading and transfer of service.

Can I sell a McMinnville house that needs repairs?

Yes. Many buyers, including cash buyers, take houses in any condition, but expect the offer to reflect the repairs. Get more than one opinion of the work needed.

Where is Newberg, Oregon?

Newberg is a Yamhill County city on the west bank of the Willamette River, about 25 miles southwest of Portland along Oregon Route 99W. It lies within the Portland metropolitan area and covers roughly 6 square miles.

Springbrook, once a separate community, is now part of the city. George Fox University sits in the city center, so the campus is part of the core neighborhoods that surround downtown.

What is Newberg's history?

Newberg grew from fur-trade and Quaker roots. Trader Ewing Young settled near Chehalem Creek in 1834, and Joseph Rogers settled the townsite in 1848, so the place was first called Chehalem and then Roger's Landing.

  • The town was platted in 1883 and incorporated in 1889.
  • Tradition says first postmaster Sebastian Brutscher named it for his former hometown of Neuberg, Germany.
  • The Newberg Graphic, the oldest surviving local paper, started December 1, 1888.
  • Quakers founded Friends Pacific Academy in 1885. It became Pacific College in 1891 and George Fox University in 1949.
  • Herbert Hoover came to Newberg in 1885 to live with his uncle and aunt, and the Hoover-Minthorn House is now a museum.

How fast has Newberg grown?

Newberg grew from 514 residents in 1890 to more than 26,000 today, and it is the second most populous city in Yamhill County. The Census Bureau estimates 26,896 residents as of July 1, 2025.

In 2020, 9,005 households lived in the city and 61.3% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. The median age was 35.2.

What employers shape the Newberg economy?

Education, health care, manufacturing and hospitality make up the local base. George Fox University and Providence Newberg Medical Center are named among the city's major employers.

  • A-dec, a dental equipment maker, was the largest employer as of 2002, with 832 employees. George Fox had 400.
  • The Allison Inn and Spa opened in September 2009 with 77 rooms and about 200 full-time workers.
  • A Hazelden Betty Ford inpatient addiction treatment center operates in the city.
  • WestRock owns the former White Birch paper facility in Newberg.
  • Portland Community College opened a campus here in 2011.

Commuters typically continue north on 99W toward Portland, so highway access is part of how a Newberg address gets described.

What is Newberg's climate and what does it do to a house?

Newberg has cool, wet winters and warm, dry summers. July is the warmest month with an average high of 80.0 degrees, while December and January highs average 46.

Rain averages 39.95 inches a year over about 152 days. Freezing temperatures occur on about 33 nights a year, with snow mainly from December through March. The record high is 107 degrees and the record low is minus 3. Water in crawl spaces, gutters that overflow, and pipes in unheated areas are the usual trouble spots for older houses here.

How do highways and the bypass affect Newberg buyers?

Oregon Route 99W runs east to west through Newberg, linking Portland to the northeast with Dundee and McMinnville to the southwest. For years that single road carried severe congestion through the Newberg-Dundee area.

The Newberg-Dundee Bypass was built to relieve it. Phase 1, a four-mile road with one lane each way from OR 219 to OR 99W south of Dundee, opened January 6, 2018. The full bypass is planned at 11 miles and a four-lane expressway, but funding so far covers Phase 1 and design of Phase 2, per the Oregon Department of Transportation. Freight moves on the Portland & Western Railroad, and regular passenger rail ended in the 1930s.

What schools serve Newberg?

Newberg-Dundee Public Schools runs six elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, Newberg High School and Catalyst Alternative High School. Private Christian schools include Veritas School and C. S. Lewis Academy.

George Fox University is classed by U.S. News & World Report as a first-tier regional university, and Portland Community College runs a campus in the city.

How does Yamhill County assess property for a Newberg house?

Yamhill County values and bills Newberg property under rules set by state law. Under ORS 308.146, taxable value is the lesser of market value and a maximum assessed value that normally rises no more than 3% a year.

That cap resets when a property is new, rebuilt or substantially altered, so a house you improved or a lot that was split may be assessed differently. Taxes are due in three parts, on November 15, February 15 and May 15. A 3% discount applies to a full payment made by November 15. Ask your title company to prorate the bill at closing. Interest of 1 1/3% per month applies to late amounts, so confirm early whether any installment is still unpaid.

What about a Newberg house that is part of an estate?

Sales by court-appointed personal representatives and trustees are excluded from Oregon's seller disclosure rules under ORS 105.470. So are sales by a financial institution that took the property through foreclosure.

Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes must provide a signed disclosure statement to each buyer who makes a written offer. If a buyer gets one, they have five business days to revoke unless they signed a waiver. Getting the right paperwork lined up first keeps an inherited sale from stalling.

How does Newberg fit into Yamhill County?

Newberg shares Yamhill County with McMinnville, Lafayette and Sheridan. The county covers 718 square miles, counted 107,722 residents in 2020, and is the fifth-smallest county in Oregon by area.

Wine is a large part of the county economy. Yamhill has more vineyard acreage than any other Oregon county, with over 80 wineries and six American Viticultural Areas wholly or partly inside its borders. Logging remains the mainstay of the western part of the county. A Newberg seller with acreage or a rural lot should ask which tax and land-use rules apply before pricing it.

What do Newberg sellers usually compare?

  • Listing with an agent versus accepting an as-is offer from a cash buyer.
  • Repair costs on an older house versus selling in present condition.
  • Closing date, tax proration and utility transfers.
  • Whether a tenant or a college renter is in the house.
  • Whether the lot is inside city limits, since city and county rules differ for rural parcels in Yamhill County.

Each buyer sets its own terms, so ask for them in writing before you decide.

More questions about Newberg, OR

What county is Newberg, Oregon in?

Newberg is in Yamhill County, in the Portland metropolitan area. McMinnville is the county seat, and Newberg is the second most populous city in the county.

How many people live in Newberg?

The Census Bureau estimates 26,896 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,138 in the 2020 census.

What is the Newberg-Dundee Bypass?

It is a planned 11-mile expressway on OR 18 meant to ease congestion on OR 99W. Phase 1, four miles, opened January 6, 2018.

When are property taxes due on a Newberg house?

November 15, February 15 and May 15. Full payment by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and two-thirds paid by then earns 2%.

Do I need a disclosure statement if I sell an inherited house in Newberg?

Not if a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, since ORS 105.470 excludes those sales. Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must provide one.

What is the median home value in Newberg?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied homes is $472,100. That is a city-wide median and not a price for any one house.
